desc:
An ongoing DevOps starter sprint is a first full round of care for your servers: updates, patches, checks and a written routine. Ecom Swift LLC reviews your set-up, fixes what it finds and leaves a plan your team can repeat.

## What is a DevOps starter sprint?

A DevOps starter sprint is a single, defined round of server maintenance that also teaches the routine. We inspect your servers and services, apply updates, check the basics and record what we did. The output is a healthier system and a checklist, not a vague promise of future support.

Servers need regular care for the same reason cars do. Operating systems release security patches, certificates approach their end dates, logs fill disks and backups drift out of date. None of this is dramatic until it is ignored for long enough.

## Why servers need regular care

Unpatched software is a common way into a system. Attackers look for known weaknesses in old versions, and a patch that sits unapplied leaves that weakness open. Disks that fill silently can stop a database. A certificate left to expire turns a working site into a browser warning.

The problem is rarely lack of skill. It is lack of routine. Small teams focus on features, and server care slips because it never feels urgent. A first care round resets the baseline, so you are working from a known, healthy state instead of an unknown one.

## How a care round improves stability

A planned round finds issues while they are cheap. Applying updates in a controlled order, with a backup first, is far calmer than patching in the middle of an incident. Checking disk, memory and certificates shows you which servers are heading toward trouble.

It also improves cost and security awareness. An uptime and cost review often shows an unused server or an oversized plan. A security settings check can show a service listening where it should not. You leave with a clear picture, a list of fixes and a routine that makes the next round shorter.

## What a good care round covers

- A health check of each server or service in scope.
- Operating system updates and security patches applied in a careful order.
- Software and runtime updates where they are safe to make.
- Disk, memory and certificate checks with simple fixes.
- A backup restore test, so you know the copies work.
- A review of logs for repeated errors and warnings.
- A basic check of security settings, such as admin access and open ports.
- An uptime and cost review for the larger package.
- A written care routine listing what to do and how often.
- A care calendar for the coming quarter, so the work is scheduled.

## How the sprint works

We start by listing your servers and services, their operating systems and what each one does. We take or confirm a backup before changing anything, then apply updates in an order that limits risk. Where a patch needs a restart, we plan it for a quiet time and tell you in advance.

After the updates, we check that everything still runs, record the state and note issues we found but did not change, with a priority. The Basic package covers one server. Standard covers several systems and adds a backup test and log review. Premium covers a broader set and adds a security, uptime and cost review with a team walkthrough.

This is a one-time round, not a monthly contract. If you want us to repeat it on a schedule, we quote that separately once we have seen what your set-up needs.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Take or confirm a backup before every round of updates.
- Patch on a schedule rather than only after a scare.
- Restart services at a quiet time and tell users first.
- Keep a short log of what was changed and when.
- Review who still has access to each server.

**Avoid:**
- Applying every update to production without a test.
- Ignoring a server because it has always worked.
- Leaving old software versions in place for years.
- Skipping the restore test of your backups.
- Letting log files grow until the disk is full.

## Who this is for

This service suits a team that has run a server for a long time and cannot remember the last update. It suits a founder who inherited servers from a former developer. It also suits a business preparing for a busy season that wants everything checked first.

## What we need from you

Send a list of your servers and services, the operating system on each and any times you cannot afford downtime. We never need your passwords. Access is given as a limited administrator, team or developer user in your own account, and keys can be removed when we finish.
